chunks: A group narrated to me, from Abu Abdullah Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ayyash, from Abu Ghalib al-Zurari, who said:

I arrived in Kufa while I was a young man, during one of my visits, and with me was a man from our brothers whose name had been forgotten by Abu Abdullah. This was during the days of Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, during his occultation, when he appointed Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, known as al-Shalmaghani. He was upright, and what later appeared from him of disbelief and heresy had not yet manifested. People would visit and meet him because he was the companion of Shaykh Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh and served as their emissary to him regarding their needs and affairs.

My companion said to me, 'Do you wish to meet Abu Ja'far and make a covenant with him, for he is the appointed one today for this group? I want to ask him for something of supplication to be written to the Hidden Imam.' I said to him, 'Yes.' We entered to him and saw a group of our companions with him, so we greeted him and sat down. He turned to my companion and asked, 'Who is this young man with you?' He said, 'A man from the family of Zurarah ibn A'yn.' He turned to me and asked, 'From which Zurarah are you?' I said, 'My master, I am from the descendants of Bakr ibn A'yn, the brother of Zurarah.' He said, 'A noble household, great in status in this matter.' My companion turned to him and said, 'Our master, I wish to write a request for supplication.' He said, 'Yes.'

When I heard this, I decided to ask for the same. I had kept in my heart a matter I had not disclosed to any of God's creation regarding the condition of my wife, the mother of my son Abu al-Abbas. She was often disagreeing and angry with me, yet I was deeply attached to her. I said to myself, 'I will ask for supplication for a matter that troubles me, without naming it.' So I said, 'May Allah prolong the life of our Master, and I have a request.' He said, 'What is it?' I said, 'Supplication for me with relief from a matter that troubles me.' He took a folder in front of him in which he recorded people's requests and wrote: 'And al-Zurari asks for supplication for him regarding a matter that has troubled him.' Then he folded it, and we rose and departed.

After a few days, my companion said to me, 'Should we not return to Abu Ja'far and ask him about the requests we made?' So I went with him and entered to him. When we sat down, he took out the folder, which contained many questions to which answers had been written in the margins. He turned to my companion and read to him the answer to his query. Then he turned to me while reading and said: 'As for al-Zurari and the condition between the husband and wife, may Allah rectify their relationship.'

He said to me, 'This matter has befallen you.' I said, 'I am amazed by it.' He said, 'Amazed by what?' I said, 'Because it was a secret that no one knew except Allah and me, and he informed me of it.' He said, 'Do you doubt the matter of the Hidden Imam? Tell me now what it is.' I told him, and he was amazed. Then it was decreed that we return to Kufa. I entered my house, and my wife, who had been angry with me and was living with her family, came to me, sought my pleasure, apologized, agreed with me, and did not disagree with me until death separated us.

key_terms.الدَّرَج: The folder or document used to record requests and responses
key_terms.الزُّرَارِيُّ: Al-Zurari (a reference to the narrator's lineage from Zurarah ibn A'yn)
key_terms.الشَّلْمَغَانِيُّ: Al-Shalmaghani (Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali, the emissary)
key_terms.النَّاحِيَةُ: The Hidden Imam (referring to the Imam in occultation)
key_terms.حَالُ الزَّوْجِ وَالزَّوْجَةِ: The condition between the husband and wife

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Abu Ghalib al-Zurari and the emissary of the Imam?
ai.summary: This narration from the Minor Occultation highlights the role of Abu Ja'far al-Shalmaghani as the primary emissary (al-Safi) between the community and Imam al-Hadi (a.s.), illustrating the mechanism of 'al-Khatm' (sealing) where specific divine knowledge is conveyed through general requests. The incident underscores the Shia belief in the Imam's omniscience regarding hidden matters, as al-Shalmaghani accurately identified the marital discord despite Abu Ghalib's silence, thereby validating the spiritual authority of the Hidden Imam.

en.sayyid-athar-husain-s-h-rizvi: H 256 - A group narrated from Abu Abdullah Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Ayyash from Abu Ghalib Zurari that he said:

“I reached Kufa. I was a young man and one of our brothers [whose name Abu Abdullah had forgotten], was with me. This was during the period of Shaykh Abul Qasim Husain Ibn Rauh, when he went into hiding and appointed Abu Ja’far Muhammad Ibn Ali known as Shalmaghani, who was at that time a righteous man and had not evinced heresy and blasphemy, which he later did. People visited him and met him, because he was a comrade of Shaykh Abul Qasim ­Husain Ibn Rauh and his emissary amongst the people with regard to their needs and necessities.

My friend said to me, “Do you wish to meet Abu Ja’far and make a covenant with him, for he is the appointed man today amongst this congregation?” I wanted to ask him to request a Dua from the Imam of the Age?” I said: “Yes.” We went to him and saw a group of our faithful brethren there with him. We offered him our greetings and sat there. He turned to my comrade and asked, “Who is this young man?” He said: “A man from the house of Zurarah.” He turned to me and asked, “Which Zurarah?” I said: “My master, I am from the children of Bukair Ibn Ayyin, brother of Zurarah.” He said: “This is a majestic household, dignified in this Order.” My comrade turned to him and said: “Our master, I want to request a Dua.” He said: “Yes.”

When I heard this, I also desired to request the same. I intended in my heart not to disclose it to anyone the condition of my wife, the mother of my son Abul Abbas. She and I had many differences and she was very angry at me, while I was greatly fond of her. I said in my heart that I will ask him a Dua for this problem that has been troubling me much. So I said: “May Allah prolong the life of our Master, I have a wish as well.” Shalmaghani said: “What is your wish?” I said: “I want a Dua for relief from a problem that has troubled me.” Shalmaghani took the paper that was in front of him on which he registered people’s requests and wrote, “And the man from Zurarah has a request for Dua about a matter that has troubled him.” Then he folded the paper. We rose and left.

After a few days, my friend said to me, “Shouldn’t we go to Abu Ja’far and ask him about the requests we made?” I went with him and we entered ­Shalmaghani’s place. As we sat down, he took out a paper that had many requests on it, which had been answered at their sides. He turned to my friend and read to him the answer of his query. Then he turned to me as he was reading, “As for the man from Zurarah and the condition between the husband and wife, may Allah rectify their relationship.”

I was overwhelmed by this great incident. We got up and left. My friend said to me, “You are overwhelmed by this?” I said: “I am amazed.” “By what?” I said: “It was a secret that no one, but God and me knew and he informed me about it.” He said: “Are you doubting the capacity of the Imam? Tell me what the story is?” I told him what had happened and he was also much amazed. Then we returned to Kufa and I went to my house. My wife, who had been angry at me and was living with her family, came and sought my pleasure and apologized to me. She remained very agreeable to me and never disagreed with me until death separated us.
